Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Refactor: split ColorettoScene god class (1808 lines) — CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV

## Problem statement

`example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` is a single-class game scene of **1808 lines** (threshold 800) that mixes rendering (rows/deck/collections, card faces, take/place animations), input handling (row click zones, mode buttons, ESC toggle), AI turn scheduling, overlay lifecycle (start, color picker, round score, game over), sound wiring, and layout math — all inside `ColorettoScene extends CardGameScene`. The size makes future changes to any one concern risky, review slow, and prevents reuse of helpers across scenes. Decompose into focused helper modules while preserving behaviour byte-for-byte.

## Users

- **Game developers extending Coloretto** — want to add features (new overlays, tweaks to the take/place animations) without wading through 1800 lines.
- **Engine maintainers** — want game-local renderer/animator/input patterns extracted so cross-game duplication can be assessed for eventual engine promotion without polluting src/.
- **Reviewers** — want smaller, concern-separated files with clear ownership when future work touches Coloretto.

### User stories

- As a developer adding a new Coloretto overlay, I can edit a small overlay helper without reading unrelated row/collection rendering and AI scheduling code.
- As a maintainer tracing a rendering bug, I can open a dedicated renderer/animator file and find the affected code without searching a god class.
- As a reviewer, I can verify that a refactor preserves behaviour via existing browser + unit coverage without re-reading the entire scene.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Renderer extracted:** Row/deck/collections rendering, card-face creation, and collection/row layout math extracted into `ColorettoRenderer` (or equivalent) in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts`; `ColorettoScene` delegates all rendering to it (scene keeps orchestration only). No rendering logic remains duplicated in the scene.
2. **Input handler extracted:** Row click handling, mode-button lifecycle, and ESC/mode toggling extracted into a `ColorettoInputHandler` (or equivalent) helper; scene delegates input wiring to it.
3. **AI scheduler extracted or reused:** AI turn sequencing (`runTurn` / delayedCall scheduling, `ai-thinking` phase transitions and the per-player `aiPlayers` wiring) moved into a dedicated AI scheduler helper (or reused from a shared base if one exists — document if reused vs newly extracted). Scene orchestrates via the helper, not inline.
4. **Behaviour preserved:** No user-visible behaviour change — all existing Coloretto tests pass (`tests/coloretto/*.test.ts`, `tests/coloretto/*.browser.test.ts`), and the scene still renders correctly at 2-5 player counts, with take/place animations, reduced-motion behaviour, Last Round card handling, and overlays. `npm run build` succeeds; `npm test -- --project unit` passes at minimum (full suite on release per quality gates).
5. **Size reduced & guard removed or updated:** `ColorettoScene.ts` is reduced below **900 lines** (half the current 1808, comfortably under the 800 + headroom rule) and the `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard comment is removed or replaced with a brief module map comment. New helper files each have a single responsibility and are referenced from the scene.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** (Scenes index / help comments / any layout notes touching the extracted modules.)
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** (Release quality gate; `npm test -- --project unit` minimum before push — see AGENTS.md.)

## Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving refactor only — no gameplay rule changes, no new features, no balance tweaks.
- Keep the scene as the single Phaser Scene entrypoint (`ColorettoScene` key) so routing/tests/screenshots remain stable.
- Prefer game-local helpers in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/` (not engine promotion) — this smell is game-local, per dedup note "Not engine-move."
- Follow the existing decomposition pattern in sibling games where applicable (e.g. `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts` + `GolfRenderer.ts` split, 310 + 346 lines) for consistency.
- SLL layout continues via `computeColorettoLayout()` / `ColorettoLayoutAdapter`; do not reintroduce hardcoded pixel positions.
- Do not break the `REFACTOR` dedup guard until filing children/parents are updated; commit message must cite `CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV`.

## Existing state

- Single file: `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — **1808 lines**, class `ColorettoScene` with ~30 private methods spanning rendering, input, AI scheduling, overlays (4 overlays), sound (SFX_KEYS + mapping), animation (take flyers, place flip), and layout helpers (`rowCenterY`, `collectionRowY`, `fixedChipStartX`, etc.).
- Companion files are already focused: `ColorettoGame.ts` (609, orchestration/rules), `ColorettoScoring.ts` (442), `ColorettoAis.ts` (216), `ColorettoCards.ts` (201), `ColorettoLayoutAdapter.ts` (81).
- `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` guard comment is present at file top (10-file REFACTOR injection, commit 173b5590).
- Detection source: `CG-0MTHTJZGM003JX8X` hybrid detection (example games & tests); parent epic `CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ`; prior god-class smell `CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI` covered different scenes (SushiGo etc.) — not a duplicate.

- Severity `low`, priority `low` — single-scene localization limits blast radius; ok to defer but tracked for when the file is next touched.

## Desired change

- Extract renderer helper(s) (`ColorettoRenderer` and optionally `ColorettoAnimator` for `playTakeAnimation`/`animatePlace`/`flipContainer`/`createFlightCard`) so row/deck/collection rendering and card-face creation live outside the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts` — God class to split (1808 lines); extract renderer/input/AI scheduler; reduce to <900 lines.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoRenderer.ts` — **New** renderer helper for rows/deck/collections, card faces, collection/row layout helpers; owned by Coloretto only.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAnimator.ts` — **New** (optional, or folded into renderer) for take/place/flip animations; owns `playTakeAnimation`/`animatePlace`/`flipContainer`/`createFlightCard`.

- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoAiScheduler.ts` — **New** (or reuse of shared AI pattern) owning `aiPlayers` + `runTurn` AI dispatch + phase bookkeeping.
- `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoLayoutAdapter.ts` — Existing SLL adapter (81 lines); renderer/animator will call into it, not duplicate it.
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoGame.ts` — Rule orchestration (609); unchanged, referenced by helpers via injected session.
- `example-games/coloretto/ColorettoAis.ts` — AI strategies (216); scheduler delegates to `ColorettoAiPlayer`/`HeuristicStrategy`.
- `tests/coloretto/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts` — Heavy browser coverage to keep green; minimal changes, scene key stays `ColorettoScene`.

## Related work

- **Parent epic:** Refactor pass (CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ) — Docs/dev/refactor-pass-CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ.md records the 16-scope inventory and filing ledger; this item is one of 4 smell children filed with 10 REFACTOR guards.
- **Sibling smell items (same epic):** Refactor: decompose MainStreet god modules — Engine 2452, Animator 1942, Renderer 1902, TurnController 1834 (CG-0MTP6KLQD001TBMH, medium) — larger MainStreet decomposition; Refactor: remove stale @typescript-eslint/no-var-requires disables in LostCitiesTextureHelpers (CG-0MTP6K42C0010G7F, completed) — precedent for low-priority refactor style.
- **Prior god-class precedent:** CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI — covered SushiGoScene etc. at different file paths; explicitly not this file (dedup passed).
- **Decomposition precedent:** `example-games/golf/scenes/GolfAnimator.ts` (310) + `GolfRenderer.ts` (346) — proves the renderer/animator split works in this codebase; follow the same naming/ownership conventions.
- **This item's guard:** `REFACTOR-CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` in `example-games/coloretto/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts:1` — to be removed/replaced on completion.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Animation timing drift (low):** Take/place tweens + reduced-motion branching must keep identical durations/easing — mitigation: run full browser suite; screenshot baselines exist under `tests/coloretto/__screenshots__/ColorettoScene.browser.test.ts`.
- **Phase lifecycle leak (low):** `PhaseManager` phase text + `animating` gate + input blocking must stay in the scene or be correctly delegated — mitigation: isolate scheduler/animator callbacks; verify illegal-click and reduced-motion tests remain green.
- **Over-extraction (medium):** Splitting too aggressively (e.g. 5 micro-helpers) adds indirection without clarity — mitigation: 2–3 helpers maximum (renderer [+animator], input, scheduler); prefer two files if animator fits inside renderer.
- **Scope creep — engine promotion:** Cross-game helper patterns (overlay, sound) are engine-move candidates but out-of-scope here (this is game-local); record any candidates as discovered-from:`CG-0MTP6KN180075VTV` work items, do not expand scope.
- **Assumptions:** No gameplay rule changes; scene key `ColorettoScene` stable; SLL via `computeColorettoLayout` preserved; tests are sufficient to catch regressions (browser suite heavy).

- Q: "What is the target decomposition?" — Answer (derived from description): Renderer, InputHandler, AI scheduler — option to fold animator into renderer; scope capped at 2–3 helpers. Source: work-item description Remediation field.
- Q: "Is this engine-move?" — Answer (derived from dedup notes): No — game-local, not promotion into src/. Source: work-item Dedup/Description + parent epic AC3 drain rationale.
- Q: "Why low priority?" — Answer (derived): Single-scene localization limits impact; extract only if/when touched. Source: work-item Severity/Description.

# One card at a time in End of Turn routines

## Problem statement

During the end-of-turn income animation, all business cards's coins animate simultaneously with minimal stagger (~60-90ms between slots), making the sequence feel instantaneous and indistinguishable. The player cannot follow which card generates how much income.

## Users

- **Main Street player**: Wants to visually follow the income calculation card-by-card during end of turn, creating a satisfying "coins rack up" moment on each card before moving to the next.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Sequential card processing**: During the base income phase, coins are counted out onto each card's grid one card at a time - card 0 completes fully before card 1 begins, card 1 before card 2, etc.
2. **Sequential coin collection**: When coins fly from grids to the HUD counter, they are processed one card at a time in slot order (card 0's coins first, then card 1's, etc.).
3. **Decreasing delay between cards**: The delay between successive cards decreases progressively (e.g., 500ms -> 400ms -> 300ms -> 200ms for a 4-card street), creating a sense of increasing speed.
4. **Faster animation per card**: The speed of individual coin animations (count-out, flight) increases with each successive card - either through shorter flight durations or reduced stagger intervals.
5. **Reduced motion preserved**: The reduced-motion mode continues to skip coin animations and only shows text progression (no change to AC8).
6. **All existing phase ordering preserved**: Phases still run in order: base -> synergy -> reputation -> events -> upcoming -> collect.
7. **Replay/headless exemption preserved**: No rendering or audio in replay mode (AC10).
8. **All unit tests pass**: Existing tests for animateIncomePhases continue to pass without modification.
9. **All browser tests pass**: The income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts suite passes, including phase ordering, coin grid population, collection, event lines, reduced motion, and replay exemption tests.

## Constraints

- **Visual change only**: The logical income calculation in applyIncome() is unchanged - this is purely about the animation timing and sequence.
- **No game state mutation**: The animation must not mutate game state (existing invariant).
- **Backward compatible**: The animateIncomePhases method signature must remain unchanged (existing callers, including tests, must work without modification).
- **Non-blocking**: Unknown/unrendered slots must still be skipped gracefully.

## Existing state

- animateIncomePhases() in MainStreetAnimator.ts processes all slots in parallel with minimal stagger (INCOME_BASE_COUNT_STAGGER_MS = 90ms for base, INCOME_FLIGHT_STAGGER_MS = 60ms for flight phases).
- Within each phase, slots.forEach() iterates all slots and dispatches animations with si * stagger offsets - resulting in near-simultaneous animation across all cards.
- Coin collection (collectIncomeGrids) iterates all grids and flies all icons in a flat loop with no slot-level sequencing.

## Desired change

Restructure animateIncomePhases() and collectIncomeGrids() to process slots sequentially within each phase, with decreasing delay between cards and increasing animation speed.

**Key files:**
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts - Primary implementation changes:
  - animateIncomePhases() - process slots sequentially within each phase
  - runIncomePhase() - accept cumulative delay offset instead of slot index
  - collectIncomeGrids() - collect one card's coins before moving to the next
- tests/main-street/income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts - May need minor timing adjustments (existing phase-ordering assertions should still pass).

## Related work

- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ: Per-phase breakdown for animated income (current phased animation system)
- CG-0MTDEAA2J001EFEF: Browser test suite for phased income animation

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: This is strictly about end-of-turn income animation. Other animations (sell, buy, event play) are out of scope.
- **Timing changes may affect test expectations**: The browser tests use waitForCondition with timeouts rather than precise timing assertions, so they should be resilient. However, the total animation duration will increase.
- **Reduced motion must remain unaffected**: The reduced-motion path (ctx.reducedMotion) must not be changed - it already skips coin animations.
- **Total duration increase**: Sequential processing will make the end-of-turn income sequence noticeably longer. This is the desired behavior per the user report.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the sequential processing apply to all phases (base, synergy, reputation, events, upcoming) or just the base phase?" - Answer (user feedback): All phases that show cards/coins should process sequentially. The user described the base case ("coins rack up on card 1, then card 2") which is the most visible; other phases should follow the same pattern for consistency.
- Q: "What exactly does 'speed of animation should increase' mean - shorter duration, or faster per-coin stagger?" - Answer (inferred from user's description): Both. The delay between successive cards should decrease, and the animation speed (coin flight/count) should feel faster on later cards.

## Plan

### Child work items

1. **Refactor runIncomePhase for sequential slot processing (CG-0MU40V8TG0024TOH)**
   - Refactor MainStreetAnimator.ts to process slots sequentially with decreasing delays
   - Update collectIncomeGrids for sequential slot-level processing
   - Add configurable timing constants for the sequential model

2. **Verify browser tests pass with sequential income animation (CG-0MU40X5CE0037YMH)**
   - Run income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts suite and verify all tests pass
   - Make minimal timing adjustments if needed
   - Optionally add sequential-processing-specific assertions
   - Depends on: CG-0MU40V8TG0024TOH

### Plan changelog

- 2026-09-16: Plan created by agent. 2 child work items created. Effort: Small, Risk: Low.

# Intake Brief — Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right (CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I)

## Problem Statement
During the Main Street end-of-turn income animation the on-card coin matrix is centred on the card and expands rightwards from the middle, obscuring card art/title and making the accumulation direction unclear. It should be left-anchored on the card face and grow strictly to the right.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants income coins clearly grouped at a consistent left-side location so card information remains legible and the coin count-up reads left→right.
- **Future example-game authors** — reuse `coin-grid` for other tableau games and expect a left-aligned packing convention.

### User Stories
- As a player, when end-of-turn income plays, I see coins accumulate starting at the left edge of each producing business card and filling rightwards, so the growth direction is predictable.
- As a player, with 1–3 coins the first coin sits at the leftmost position, not in the centre of the card.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Default coin-grid anchor is on the left side of the business card (not the centre / bottom-right quadrant), with the grid's left edge aligned to the card's left inset and growth proceeding rightwards (row-major, left→right, top→bottom).
- [ ] `packCoins` (and any browser rendering via `createCoinGrid`) is left-aligned: for N icons the first placement is at the left edge (`w/2` from the grid origin) and additional icons extend to the right without re-centring earlier icons. Verified for 1, 3, 5, 10, 15+ icons.
- [ ] Packing behaviour (columns 5 → 10 → 15, shrink then overlap, height-fit scaling) is preserved under the new left-aligned layout; coins remain fully inside `availableWidth`/`availableHeight`.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; existing `coin-grid.test.ts` / `coin-grid.browser.test.ts` expectations updated to the left-aligned contract.

## Constraints
- Reuse existing `coin-grid.ts` texture/metrics (`COIN_GRID_SIZE=10`, `COIN_GRID_SPACING=2`, `MIN_COIN_SIZE=4`); do not introduce a second grid component.
- Presentation-only change — no mutation of `SlotPhaseBreakdown` or credited income totals.
- Must work with the current Phaser 4 card containers (centre-origin cards) and `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` lifecycle (`reducedMotion` path retained).
- Keep API compatible or provide a migration for explicit `anchorX`/`anchorY` callers (Animator currently calls `createCoinGrid(s, card)` with defaults).

## Existing State
- `packCoins` computes placements relative to the grid centre (`col*(w+s) - finalGridW/2 + w/2`) and the grid container is anchored at `cardW/4, cardH/4` (bottom-right quadrant centre) with `availableWidth=cardW/2`. A 1-coin case therefore renders near the card centre, not the left edge.
- `createCoinGrid` is consumed only by `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` (with defaults), so callers are centralised.
- Packing and rendering are covered by `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts`; VFX scaling (`iconsForAmount`) is in `coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts`.

## Desired Change
- Move the default grid anchor to the left side of the card (e.g., `availableWidth≈cardW - inset*2` and `anchorX≈ -cardW/2 + inset + availableWidth/2` or an equivalent left-aligned container placement) and make `packCoins` left-aligned so placements start at `w/2` and grow rightwards. Update comments/tests accordingly. Alternative implementations that achieve the same visual (left edge start, rightward growth, no centre bias) are acceptable if they keep the grid inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — `packCoins` layout math and `createCoinGrid` default anchor/region; update layout formula and default geometry + doc comments
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — sole `createCoinGrid` consumer; verify default call still correct, no per-slot override needed
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — card container geometry (`slotW/slotH`, `cardContainer` origin) for anchor verification
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` — pure packing assertions (centre vs left alignment)
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.browser.test.ts` — Phaser wrapper assertions
- `tests/main-street/coin-vfx-scaling.test.ts` — unaffected but nearby regression surface

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:** `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` header comment (packing policy), `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` (phased income choreography)
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `On-card coin grid rendering + packing (CG-0MTDE9H0C0061D51)` — completed — introduced `packCoins`/`createCoinGrid`; its packing/anchor defaults are the bug location
  - `Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD) (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE)` — completed — income flight lifecycle that now uses the grid
  - `End-of-turn VFX/SFX scaled to x100 economy (CG-0MTK2JHXD004KNQI)` — completed — presentation scaling (`iconsForAmount`) layered atop the grid
  - `Coins do not reliably stay on the card (CG-0MTQ7NI63001R55C)` — open — nearby reliability concern for coin containment
  - `Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q)` — open — end-of-turn timing context

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Visual regression risk:** moving the anchor leftwards could clip or overlap card title/art on narrow cards — mitigate by choosing an inset that keeps coins in the lower-left inset and verifying against `FALLBACK_CARD_W/H`.
- **Test churn:** existing unit/browser tests assert centre-relative placements — mitigate by updating expectations to the left-aligned contract explicitly in the same change.
- **Scope creep:** temptation to restyle the whole income animation — out of scope; record any broader animation polish as separate work items.
- **Assumption:** "left side" means left-aligned within the card face (lower-left region), growing rightwards row-major, with vertical placement in the lower half; if producer meant a different inset, the same left→right contract applies and the exact Y/inset can be tuned during implementation without changing ACs.

## Open Questions
- None — seed context is sufficient for a clear brief. Assumed lower-left placement; implementation can tune Y/inset and confirm during review. No clarifying interview required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work item description ("coin matrix in the end turn should be positioned on the left side of the card and grow to the right. At present they start in the middle and grow right.") plus repo inspection of `coin-grid.ts` packing/anchor provided sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for documented inset/Y assumptions.

## Plan: Changelog

### 2026-09-20 — Plan created by Map (AI agent)
- **Decision:** Full planning required (effort: Small, risk: Low — pre-check returned `plan`, not `skip`). No approval gate required.
- **Approach:** 3 child tasks in dependency chain:
  1. **CG-0MU9JVGNM0051ZVA** — Refactor `packCoins` to left-align coin placements (core logic change)
  2. **CG-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J** — Update `createCoinGrid` defaults to left-anchored position (anchor + available region)
  3. **CG-0MU9K00HO009I2QC** — Update coin-grid tests and documentation (test assertions + doc comments)
- **Key design decision:** `packCoins` X formula changes from centre-relative (`col*(w+s) - finalGridW/2 + w/2`) to left-aligned (`col*(w+s) + w/2`). Default anchorX changes from `cardW/4` to `-cardW/2 + leftInset` (default 8px). Default availableWidth changes from `cardW/2` to `cardW - leftInset*2`. anchorY stays at `cardH/4`.
- **Vertical slice:** Each task is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs) of the same change surface, executed in dependency order. No horizontal layering needed for this small scope.
- **No interview conducted** — the seed context (work item description + repo inspection) was sufficient.

Each child has a clear goal + measurable ACs. **No test file is deleted by this child — only recommendations are created.**

## Anti-pattern taxonomy (from CG-0MS9AGG3N003ASCR)
- **source-code-grep**: assert the text of source files (readFileSync + toContain/string index on .ts files), break on any refactor, never detect behavioral regressions

- **self-referential simulations**: import zero production code, test only their own structure
- **duplicates of core coverage**: test something already tested by a deeper core-engine test
- **type-level/structural-only**: assert factory returns N fields the compiler already enforces
- **zero-assertion browser tests**: browser tests with no `expect()` calls

## Notes
